newsitem.title: USA: Stocks soar with Dow Average up 104 points to record.
newsitem.headline: Stocks soar with Dow Average up 104 points to record.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average jumped more than 100 points to a new high Tuesday as investors expressed confidence about the outlook for the economy and second-quarter earnings.

The 30-share Dow rose 103.82 points, or 1.32 percent, to 7,962.31, putting it less than 38 points from the 8,000 mark. It was the 30th record this year for the world's most widely watched stock index, whose previous record of 7,895.81 came on Thursday.
Broader market averages also hit new highs.

The Nasdaq composite index jumped 14.36 points to 1,485.10, its fourth consecutive record, on strong gains in technology stocks. The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 6.55 points to 918.75 and the NYSE composite index rose 2.94 to 478.49, both records.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,680 to 1,122 on active volume of 525 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"Eight thousand is a foregone conclusion at this point," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "We've been hemming and hawing just below 8,000 and the next time we make a move we'll probably blast right through."

So-called cyclical stocks that are most sensitive to swings in the economy paced the advance among blue chips, with International Paper Co. jumping 4-11/16 to 56 after reporting second quarter earnings that beat Wall Street estimates.
International Paper was the second Dow component to beat analysts' estimates in as many days, following Monday's of stronger-than-expected earnings from Aluminum Co. of America.

Investors quickly seized on the good news, bidding up International Paper and other so-called cyclical issues after largely shunning the group earlier this year over concerns over the potential economic impact of possible interest rate increases by the Federal Reserve.
With rate fears now mostly out of the picture, analysts said economically sensitive stocks were back in favour.

"Cyclicals had really underperformed year-to-date and from a valuation standpoint many of them were attractive compared to the Cokes and GEs," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest. "We're starting to see money rotate back to them now."
Good profits from the first few companies to report only added to optimism as the earnings period gets into full swing, analysts said.

"Judging from the market, most people are looking for good numbers," said Peter Canelo, U.S. equity strategist at Morgan Stanley Dean Witter. "It surprised me that we didn't have more pre-announcement warnings," he said. "That led me to think the numbers this quarter are going to be pretty good."
Motorola Inc. jumped 2-7/16 to a year-high 82-13/16 ahead of the release of its earnings, which were reported after the close.
Among other individual issues, Procter & Gamble Co. jumped 5-7/8 to 150 after announcing a 2-for-1 stock split, an increase in its dividend and a $1 billion stock buyback.
There were market soft spots. Several small network software companies tumbled after announcing that second quarter results would fail to match expectations.
Among them, XcelleNet Inc. tumbled five to 8-7/8, Wall Data Inc. slid 9-7/8 to 17-7/8, Segue Software Inc. fell 4-7/16 to 8-11/16 and Dataworks Corp. lost 6-1/4 to 13-1/4.
The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.14 points to 634.11. The average NYSE share gained 27 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues also known as the Wilshire 5,000 -- hit a new high of 8,670.441, up 59.585 or 0.69 percent.
